turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_fatigue_train.csv: 293 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si,
    Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and `target` (the
    measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).
  - b3_fatigue_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose rotating-bending
    fatigue strength (MPa) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the
    same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST rotating-
bending fatigue strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**1. The dominant factor is the process route, not composition.**

Grouping the training set by process signature:

| Process group (NT/THT/CT/TT…) | typical target |
|---|---|
| Normalized only (885, TT=30) | 232–275 |
| Q&T 865/845/825 °C, TT 550–650 | 325–540 |
| Q&T with Cr≈1 or Ni≈1.7–2.7 alloys, TT 550–680 | 460–645 |
| Low-temper spring-type steels (845/845, TT 420–500, high C, high Si) | 680–906 |
| **Carburized route (CT = 930, Ct > 0, DT ≈ 850–900, QmT 60–140, TT 160–200)** | **838–1144** |

So the carburized candidates dominate everything else; all pool candidates with `CT=930, Ct>0` are the only serious contenders (c000, c016, c018, c046, c050, c053, c054, c062, c063, c075, c081).

**2. Within the carburized group, the drivers are:**
- **Alloying:** Ni≈1.6–1.7 (+Mo≈0.2) or Cr≈1.1–1.2 (+Mo≈0.17) give the top values (1034–1144); Ni≈0.45, Cr≈0.5 grades sit lower (~880–1090 but averaging ~960–1000).
- **Carburizing time Ct:** longer/intermediate Ct (340–510 min) beats very short Ct (90–140 min) by ~50–70 MPa.
- **QmT:** QmT = 60 beats QmT = 140 by roughly 60 MPa (e.g. Cr1.17: 1144 vs 1080).
- **TT:** 200 °C temper is slightly worse than 160 °C (≈ −20 to −60 MPa).

**3. Candidate estimates (carburized set):**

| id | key features | estimate |
|---|---|---|
| c081 | Cr1.17/Mo0.17, Ct340, QmT60, TT200 (twin of the 1144 record) | ≈1090 |
| c053 | Ni1.69/Cr0.55/Mo0.18, Ct140, QmT60, TT160 | ≈1070 |
| c016 | Ni1.64/Mo0.16, Ct470, QmT60, TT200 (twin of 1082) | ≈1060 |
| c063 | Ni1.62/Cr0.59/Mo0.21, Ct470, QmT60, TT160 | ≈1050 |
| c046 | Ni0.44/Cr0.60, Ct450, Dt34.8, QmT60, TT160 (twin of 1009/1033) | ≈1035 |
| c018 | Ni1.62, Ct470, QmT60, TT200 | ≈1030 |
| c062 | Ni1.64, Ct140, TT160 | ≈1030 |
| c054/c050/c075/c000 | leaner alloys or QmT140 | ≈965–995 |

Non-carburized best (c094: 0.61C–2.05Si, TT500 ≈ 860; c052 ≈ 805; c019 ≈ 850) fall clearly below the carburized leaders.

**Final: c081, c053, c016, c063, c046**
